definition: UBY is a large-scale lexical-semantic resource for natural language processing (NLP) developed at the Ubiquitous Knowledge Processing Lab (UKP) in the department of Computer Science of the Technische Universität Darmstadt .
details: UBY is based on the ISO standard Lexical Markup Framework (LMF) and combines information from several expert-constructed and collaboratively constructed resources for English and German. UBY applies a word sense alignment approach (subfield of word sense disambiguation) for combining information about nouns and verbs. Currently, UBY contains 12 integrated resources in English and German.

explainer.lead: UBY is a large-scale lexical-semantic resource for NLP that combines information from several expert-constructed and collaboratively constructed resources for English and German. It matters because it unifies word information that would otherwise be scattered.

tiers.eli5: Like one big dictionary assembled from many dictionaries, with the entries lined up so they mean the same thing.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers rely on UBY for combined noun and verb information via word sense alignment; a pitfall is that alignment quality bounds how well the merged resources agree.
tiers.paperLevel: Based on the ISO standard Lexical Markup Framework and built at the Ubiquitous Knowledge Processing Lab; it applies a word sense alignment approach to combine noun and verb information and currently contains 12 integrated resources in English and German.

explainer.example: A system queries UBY for sense information on an English noun and gets information merged from the 12 integrated resources.
